67.t: More Chicago names: Mae Brady, Elliott Washington, Bertha Gonzalez
67.s: Albertson runs through violinists and a pianist; Cheatham mostly did not know them.
67.ch: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
67.q: I remember that name, yes. I remember that name, Elliott Washington, yes.

67.t: Albertson tests his memory of early Chicago names
67.s: Cheatham recognizes Roy Palmer, the Pioneer Club and Curtis Moseby but did not know many others, being wrapped up in music.
67.ch: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
67.q: At that time, you know, I was so wrapped up in music, so much that I didn't attend any of those type of places.

251.t: Alan, and Syke Collins in Chicago
251.s: Brief talk of a musician who just missed meeting the interviewer, and Syke's real name and whereabouts.
251.q: Yes, I wanted you to meet him, but, uh, something slipped up here where he didn't get a chance to meet him. He had a time associated.

252.t: Pianist Walter Johnson who died in India, versus Teddy Weatherford
252.s: Boote recalls pianist Walter Johnson, who played with Tate in Chicago and married an Indian princess; Allen suggests Teddy Weatherford.
252.q: this piano player, Walter Johnson, he died over in India somewhere. He married an Indian prince. He was... He used to play with Tate in Chicago. I know.

401.t: Tom Zimmerman and other names from the union magazine
401.s: The interviewer asks about various names; Williams recalls Tom Zimmerman, a heavy-drinking piano player at Tom Anderson's.
401.q: at Tom Anderson for a while. He was a heavy drinker. He played a nice piano. I remember him. Yeah I still see

664.s: Reel three opens; he did not know the Fort Myers well and suggests asking Cats.
664.q: Yeah, the Fort Myers, they played around the time I was playing. I didn't know them very well. Cats played with them. They come a little after me, after I quit playing, I think, because I heard of them, and I know Cats played with them. We'll get to ask Cats about them. Yeah, you'd have to ask…

191.t: Allen asks about Mobile players in that band
191.s: Allen names Avery Loposa and Felix Carino; Kelly did not know them.
191.q: Ha ha. Well, I'm certainly glad we finally got together. Oh, yeah.

665.t: Zeb whose last name no one remembers
665.s: Everyone remembers Zeb, nobody his surname.
665.q: I can't say Zeb's last name, but that's his people over the street. There's some of his cousins and things.

666.t: Jinx Dybal, the architect who was the worst musician
666.s: After a mix-up with another Dybal, Rau recalls the architect Jinx as the band's weakest musician, whom Fred Ogden coached on chord changes.
666.q: Dybal, yeah, that's right. He was with us way back there, and so long ago I can't remember him too well. What did he play? He wasn't playing any music as far as I remember. I'm talking about we had a Dybal that worked for us in this company. I think he was in the stock department.

198.t: Where Blind Charlie is now, and his missing last name
198.s: The group tries to identify Blind Charlie, whom Barnes met a year ago, and Barnes explains musicians are known by first names only.
198.ch: Blind Charlie, kin and early memories
198.q: We don't know who he is or anything. He's a blind fellow. He was playing clowns years ago. He was a good clown player but he goes around right now. If he ain't dead.

367.t: Guessing the violinist who joined Carter's band
367.s: Young cannot recall the name of a violin-playing friend who joined the band out of Boston; Brown and Kimery offer wrong guesses.
367.q: No, we never got to play the Apollo. That's when that violin player, famous violin player, joined Chick Carter‘s band. And he went onto play with…

377.s: Basie says he does not remember Katie Crippen at all and Kuehl plans to ask May.
377.ch: Carnegie Hall, nicknames and later career
377.q: I don't know what -- I don't remember Katie Crippen at all.

231.t: Crossing paths with the Ritz Brothers, Marx Brothers and others
231.s: Asked about future stars met in vaudeville he names Tony DeMarco, the Ritz and Marx Brothers but recalls no stories.
231.ch: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
231.q: No, I had that with Tony DeMarco and Sally -- and what's that last name -- I forgot her last name. However, Tony DeMarco and Ritz Brothers and --

611.t: Charlie Gaines and Charlie James gigs in Philadelphia
611.s: Waters clarifies that a trumpeter was better known rather than better, identifies Charlie Gaines, and recalls commercial gigs with Gaines and with Charlie James of the Black union.
611.ch: Other Philadelphia work and the union
611.q: Oh no, not - more famous, no, I didn't say famous, I didn't say famous musically - no, we got it wrong there, Phil. I didn't say more famous musically, I said more known.
